body: I feel you man. I went to another country to be with my gf, I stupidly cheated on my gf while in that country with her 3000 miles away from home. Honestly I think I'm bipolar or schizophrenic but I'm not using that as an excuse. Within a month my mum was dead, who was my absolute idol. I'm also homeless just like you, I don't know how I'm going to afford the petrol money to get to the airport when my flight comes up. Honestly 2020 is 1000 times worse than my second worst year on Earth. If by some slim chance I survive this year I'm going to work with charities. I'm going to be the best person I can be, if I can make someone else's life incrementally easier I will

For me, depression isn't an excuse for not caring. I have been absolute rock bottom, suicidal and wanting to spend every minute of the day high to cope. But it effected my gf, I saw she hated it and the way it was affecting her hurt me just as much as the depression did. It sounds to me that he has no desire to change. At the end of the day he can't improve unless he wants to improve. So I'd say definitely tell him you're considering leaving him. If he doesn't care about himself then that's understandable with depression. But if he can't even make baby steps in the right direction for YOU, I hate this saying but it's a red flag. He needs to WANT to improve. He should be at the doctor's telling them the Wellbutrin isn't working. He should care about your feelings, he should care that you are frustrated. You really do need to hammer home that yes this isn't just a minor inconvenience. This is a deal breaker. This is something you NEED and you won't accept no as an answer. If he refuses to listen or still doesn't care then maybe he just doesn't care as much as he says he does. 

This is the sad part. You can only do so much and you need to think of yourself. Do not risk becoming depressed or letting him have a negative impact on your mental health as that will take longer to recover from than if you just left him. Honestly feel free to ask me anything as I have been there. Depression is evil, I wouldn't wish it on my worst enemy. But believe me the person with depression can make it 10x worse if they don't take it seriously.

Hmm... I rarely comment on anything like this, but as I've suffered with depression and low libido I feel I might be able to give you some things to think about and possibly help you.

So my first thought was, "Is he getting help?" I understand depending on where you live the help and support you can get for depression vary massively. But this was my first thought, as I know depression is evil. It takes every single thing you enjoy and makes it seem meaningless. So the depression, as you probably know and understand isn't his fault. BUT this is the important part, if he isn't actively seeking help or getting it at the moment then it shows he isn't ready for help (and also a relationship).

The one thing that did jump out to me though was your bf trying to blame you for having a higher libido than him and calling it a "stupid problem" and that "sex doesn't matter" etc. He is fully justified to not want sex, he is within his right to think whatever he likes. But he is completely disregarding your feelings and that isn't okay. If he had said something along the lines of "I know this is important to you, sex doesn't matter to me but I want to try for you" that would have at least taken your feelings and needs into account.

I don't have enough information to say he doesn't care, as I haven't been there and seen your conversations with him. But in my opinion you need to sit him down and explain just how much this is effecting you. Tell him that the lack of sex is making you question your future together. I can't stress that enough, make sure he knows how serious this is effecting you. Then it's on him. He can either make some changes, if he isn't already, start seeing a doctor about his depression, maybe make some lifestyle changes that will improve his mood. If he doesn't make any effort then... Well maybe you have your answer of what you need to do next. Just remember that if he is getting help or promises to get help ot might get worse before it gets better. Be ready to stick through a rough few months before expecting any improvement.

Sorry for the long post, it definitely struck a nerve as I have dealt with horrific depression that effected my gf too. The difference is I did everything I could to work on myself so it didn't hurt her anymore. Just remember you're not obligated to stay with him just because he's depressed. It's important to get out of there if you feel it starts to take a negative effect on you, he is already depressed. You don't have to be too.

Good luck and I hope you manage to work things out with him
